recap.text: Carl sprays over the name Death Trap on the captured Drop Bear, writes Nightmare II on its side, and rips off both armrests to fit the pilot's seat. Louis and Firas lash the plane down in the garage, and Carl flies it off the edge of the yard, his Biplane Pilot skill rising to three. He throws a celestial grenade at Quan and jumps, and the spiralling plane hits Emberus in the nose and explodes.

beats.headline: Death Trap, painted over
beats.text: The others secured an intact Drop Bear, its pilot nowhere to be found, and Langley had it covered with a tarp before the storm. It runs on actual gasoline. Carl fills the tank only a quarter of the way to keep it light, and there are no bombs left under the wings. On the nose, over a frothing, rabid koala, the stencilled name reads Death Trap, with four bombs painted after it. Carl sprays over it and writes Nightmare II on the side. Donut objects, but only half-heartedly. He has to rip off both armrests to fit in the pilot's seat.
beats.gist: Carl sprays over the name Death Trap on the Drop Bear and writes Nightmare II.

beats.headline: Up on the emergency balloons
beats.text: There is no runway. Donut takes the rear-facing gunner's chair and makes shooting noises. Carl yanks the lever beside his seat like a car's emergency brake, the twin emergency balloons hiss full, and the plane jerks upward tail first; on the way up Donut finds there are still bullets in the gun, and don't you dare, says Carl. At the ceiling of the bubble, about five kilometres above the bowl, the plane, still tied to its balloons, skitters along on its engines like a bicycle on training wheels toward the glowing balloon of the flying house. Donut jumps from her seat onto its net, and Carl follows from the nose.
beats.gist: Carl yanks the lever, the balloons hiss full, and the plane jerks up tail first.

beats.headline: Back down on its own
beats.text: Marching back to Hump Town, Donut spots the airplane slowly descending from the sky. It is the Nightmare II. It came loose from the main balloon during the boss fight, and its emergency balloon has finally lost its juice and is letting it down. Carl sends Louis and Firas out to secure it and drag it back to the house. It should fit in the large garage, safe from the next storm, and it will give them something to do.
beats.gist: Louis and Firas go out to drag the fallen Nightmare II back to the house garage.

beats.headline: Off the edge of the yard
beats.text: Louis and Firas lashed the biplane down in the garage, the only part of the flying house that still has a roof. Now they all pull it out of the garage facing the wind, and Donut sits at the gun behind Carl, sticking her Torch spell under the top wing to light both cockpits. Carl barely knows what he is doing: yoke, pedals, a fuel gauge, a gyroscope he does not understand, twin throttles. He pushes the throttle, and the little biplane rolls off the edge of the yard and drops like a rock until flying into the wind lets him pull up over the ocean. His Biplane Pilot skill rises to three.
beats.gist: Carl pilots the biplane off the yard's edge, drops, then pulls up over the ocean.

beats.headline: Into the nose of a god
beats.text: Quan has knocked Orthrus unconscious at two percent and is moving in to finish him. Carl dives the Nightmare II at the dog, tells Donut to grab the stick, and from the wing throws a potion ball of Mordecai's Special Brew that tops the puppy's health back up. Donut, paws locked on the yoke, loops the plane twice; something falls off the back, and the pedals break. Carl gets it out of its roll but not its spiral. He chooses to worship Emberus, and from the top wing he throws the celestial grenade at Quan and jumps. Emberus appears above them, a city-sized floating head, and the spiralling Drop Bear hits him right in the nose and explodes.
beats.gist: Quan nearly kills Orthrus; Carl heals him, then jumps, and the spiralling Drop Bear explodes on Emberus's nose.
